# DKR-003: Docker socket is not world writable

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** critical
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

Whoever can write to /var/run/docker.sock controls the daemon, which is root on the host. A world writable socket makes every local user, and every service account an attacker lands in, root. stackward reads the socket's metadata only. This check can fail without access to the Docker socket.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls -l /var/run/docker.sock
```

## How to fix it

Restore the default: chown root:docker /var/run/docker.sock && chmod 660 /var/run/docker.sock, then find what changed it (often a chmod 666 in a setup script or a unit override) and remove that.

## What a fix can break

Users and services that relied on the open socket need to be in the docker group (which is also root equivalent) or use a socket proxy.

Run `stackward explain DKR-003` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
